PLANT-1.claim: Across studies of interactive learning environments, good help-seeking predicts better learning, yet learners typically do not use on-demand help facilities effectively.

PLANT-2.claim: A meta-analysis of psychology classrooms found that testing during the learning phase benefited later retrieval from long-term memory.

PLANT-3.claim: In an ASR-based Dutch reading tutor for first-grade pupils, both explicit and implicit feedback improved reading accuracy, while explicit feedback was more beneficial for accuracy gains in reading sentences.

PLANT-4.claim: Naturalistic one-to-one tutoring prominently features collaborative problem solving, question answering, and explanation within specific examples.

PLANT-5.claim: A selective review found that effective help-seeking in interactive learning environments is related to better learning outcomes, but learners often do not use help facilities effectively.

PLANT-6.claim: In a study of first-grade pupils using an ASR-based Dutch reading tutor, both explicit and implicit feedback improved reading accuracy, while explicit feedback was more beneficial for sentence-reading accuracy.

PLANT-7.claim: Prompt injection is a leading, catalogued security risk for LLM applications because inputs can alter model behavior in unintended ways.

PLANT-8.claim: A selective review found that effective help-seeking behavior in interactive learning environments is related to better learning outcomes, although learners often do not use help facilities effectively.
